identity: BAS Animal Sciences; English-taught academic bachelor;2026–2027 Animal Management and Care, MathA-preparation and first-listed livestock restricted option; no named minor selected.

components.name: Introduction to Cell Biology
components.finding: Shared cell structure, membranes, signalling, gene regulation and bioenergetics. WUR includes its own cell/biochemical laboratory practicals; UCR’s Molecular Cell Biology emphasises molecular mechanisms and research appraisal.

components.name: Introduction to Animal Sciences
components.finding: No selected course integrates the full animal-sciences orientation across species, behaviour/ecology, production and health. Shared cellular/ecological contributions remain separately identified.

components.name: Fundamentals of Evolutionary Genetics
components.finding: Shared Mendelian, population/quantitative and evolutionary genetics, variation and selection. WUR additionally develops detailed molecular genetic problems and case exercises; UCR develops broader evolutionary history and Tinbergen analysis.

components.name: Statistics 2
components.finding: Shared statistical estimation, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing, grounded in probability and simulation at UCR. WUR additionally develops simple applied regression for life-science data; the advanced-statistics award remains separate.

components.name: Biology of Domestic Animals
components.finding: No selected course reproduces domestic-animal production biology, live-animal phenotype measurements, feeding/housing, lactation and comparative practical cases.

components.name: Mathematics Applied: Analysis
components.finding: Shared differentiation, integration, differential equations and mathematical modelling. UCR adds dynamic population/predator–prey modelling; the prior-preparation introduction and separate linear-algebra award remain distinct.

components.name: Bio-organic Chemistry for Life Sciences
components.finding: No adequate whole counterpart for bio-organic reactions, stereochemistry and natural-product structure/reactivity. Biochemistry is most strongly aligned to nutrient metabolism.

components.name: Zoology (English)
components.finding: UCR Functional Anatomy studies human anatomy. WUR’s Zoology additionally develops comparative vertebrate form, evolution/development, histology and animal practicals.

components.name: General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
components.finding: Shared chemical equilibrium, molecular/energy principles and thermodynamics. UCR uses environmental/material contexts and does not reproduce the complete life-science buffer, kinetics and ATP-coupling sequence.

components.name: Dilemmas in Animal Management and Care
components.finding: Shared ethical theory/argument and independent position on practical moral responsibility, including animal-rights applications at UCR. WUR specifically analyses animal management practices and their welfare/sustainability dilemmas.

components.name: Animal Behaviour
components.finding: UCR Neurobiology includes animal behaviour, welfare and comparative neural mechanisms. WUR adds dedicated ethological observation, Tinbergen’s questions and behavioural-data collection.

components.name: Mathematics Applied: Linear Algebra
components.finding: No selected dedicated vectors/matrices/eigenvalues/linear-algebra course; current Mathematical Methods detailed content is calculus/dynamic modelling.

components.name: Internship
components.finding: WUR requires practical animal handling, feeding and housing training plus an individual husbandry internship. The UCR classroom/laboratory courses do not supply this placement.

components.name: Animal Breeding and Genetics
components.finding: Evolutionary and human genetic mechanisms do not reproduce designing and optimising livestock/companion-animal breeding programmes.

components.name: Human and Animal Physiology
components.finding: Normal organ-system regulation is shared. UCR focuses on human physiology; WUR includes comparative animal morphology, histology and physiological practicals.

components.name: Immunology and Thermoregulation
components.finding: Shared host-defence and inflammatory mechanisms are a partial correspondence. WUR additionally integrates animal housing/climate stress, immunology and thermoregulation.

components.name: Veterinary Epidemiology and Economics
components.finding: Epidemiological risk/design/causality methods are shared; UCR studies human public health, while WUR integrates animal disease-control decisions and veterinary economics.

components.name: Principles of Animal Nutrition
components.finding: Biochemistry shares nutrient chemistry and energy metabolism. WUR adds animal-specific requirements, feed formulation/manufacture, chemical feed/faeces analysis and live-animal trials.

components.name: Systems Approach in Animal Sciences
components.finding: Shared sustainability assessment, production-system impacts and circular-resource reasoning. WUR integrates systems/linear-programming and qualitative methods in a livestock case; UCR develops product/process life-cycle assessment.

components.name: Introduction to Animal Ecology
components.finding: Shared environmental conditions/resources, population dynamics, predation, competition and food webs, with quantitative ecological modelling. WUR focuses on animals, ecological-requirement projects and wildlife observation.

components.name: Advanced Statistics
components.finding: Shared multiple regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures models, assumptions and R-based data interpretation. Applications and exact inferential scope differ.

components.name: Skills Academy and Personal Assessment
components.finding: Skills Academy is a 3 EC continuous portfolio across all 3 years, concluding alongside the thesis. UCR’s PPD develops shared academic/reflection skills in Year 1; the structures differ.

components.name: Quantitative Skills for Animal Sciences
components.finding: Exploratory data preparation, visualisation and R scripting are shared. WUR additionally connects advanced statistical models and assumption checks to animal data and uses Excel.

components.name: Mathematics Applied: Introduction
components.finding: This example selects Mathematics Applied: Introduction for VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; other educational backgrounds choose with the study adviser.

components.name: Aquaculture Biology
components.finding: UCR Marine Biology studies ecosystems, fisheries/aquaculture and human impacts; it does not reproduce the cultivation physiology and practicals required by Aquaculture Biology.

components.name: Introduction to Business Economics, Management and Marketing
components.finding: Shared business-environment analysis, marketing/finance/operations and an integrated business plan. WUR applies planning to a food-supply-chain enterprise; UCR develops a new-venture concept.

components.name: Reproduction and Fertility
components.finding: General human reproductive anatomy/physiology does not reproduce farm/companion-species fertility cycles, management and reproductive technologies.

components.name: Infections and Disorders
components.finding: The additional animal-management/inflammation/metabolic/behavioural disorder sequence remains separate; shared host defence is aligned to Immunology and Thermoregulation.

components.name: Role of Livestock in Future Food Systems
components.finding: This example chooses Role of Livestock in Future Food Systems from the 6 EC restricted cluster. Fish/seafood sustainability or Companion Animals are alternatives, not added requirements.

components.name: BSc Thesis Animal Sciences
components.finding: WUR requires an individual 12 EC animal-sciences thesis with proposal, research, written report, presentation and defence. Formal intake requires 102 compulsory/restricted credits including all 60 first-year credits; Advanced Statistics and Skills Academy are taken before or alongside the thesis. Optional UCR 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.

entryAndProgression: Current BAS is an English-taught, three-year academic bachelor in applied animal biology: livestock, companion, aquatic and wild animals, from cells to systems, with health/welfare, genetics, nutrition, behaviour/ecology and sustainability. The programme overview explicitly distinguishes it from a veterinary/practical-care qualification; actual credited modules nevertheless include hands-on research/handling and an internship. Neither fact cancels the other.

Full LC group descriptions control selection: choose all common courses, even where individual legacy required flags are false. All positive compulsory awards total111EC. Three safety modules and the continuous Brightspace registration are0EC obligations, not credits. Choose the3EC prior-preparation module and required12EC thesis to obtain126commonEC.

First route in both official programme and handbook is Animal Management and Care, independent of UCR fit. All four required route courses total18EC. Its restricted cluster requires6EC; select first-listed Role of Livestock in Future Food Systems. Fish/Seafood Sustainability and Companion Animals are alternatives, not extra requirements. Biological Functioning of Animals is the unselected route; its laboratory/immunotechnology/virology modules are not imported into this pathway.

Use the MathA-preparation example: MAT14803 for VWO MathematicsA, MAT15303 Statistics1 for MathematicsB. Other backgrounds choose with the adviser. This is a preparation-dependent rule, not a UCR-driven source-order choice. MAT15403 assumes active high-school statistics/MathA or Statistics1; MAT15103/15203 assume introductory mathematics or MathB. Keep the introduction, applied analysis, linear algebra, Statistics2 and advanced statistics as separate awards.

Current programme phases establish57B1common+3choice=60B1;42B2common+18route=60B2;12B3common+6restricted+12thesis+30electives=60B3. Thus150specified credits plus30genuine elective/minor credits=180, without double counting or invented elective subject packages. Common credits111+choice3+thesis12=126; route18+6=24.

The required individual12EC thesis has formal examiner intake and requires102compulsory/restricted credits including all60B1. Complete all120B1/B2 before it. AdvancedStatistics and SkillsAcademy are allowed before or alongside thesis. YAS21303 is a continuous3EC portfolio spanning all3years, concluded with the thesis; its0EC Brightspace predecessor is not an extra award.

Thesis runs half-time in P1+2 or P5+6 with6ECother study in each period. A coherent B3 allocation is AdvancedStatistics6+SkillsAcademy3+electives3 in P1;QuantitativeSkills3+electives9 in P2;Livestock6 in P3;electives6 in P4;thesis12+electives12 across P5+6. The portfolio records thesis reflection at completion; it is not falsely required to be finished before thesis. This uses real period offerings and leaves elective subjects open.

Thesis assessment metadata: report50%, oral presentation/defence20%, research competence30%, each minimum5.50. Current content requires individual research, proposal, written thesis, oral presentation and defence; the overview specifies an animal dataset. No taught group meta-analysis is equated to the individual original animal-data project.

Laboratory safety precedes the named cell/chemistry/zoology/physiology/nutrition/aquaculture/reproduction practicals; fieldwork safety precedes AnimalEcology. Advisory foundations for genetics, breeding, physiology, immunology/thermoregulation, veterinary epidemiology, quantitative analysis and the livestock option were inspected separately from hard requirements. All B1/B2 completed first meets these progression needs.

Internship is6EC, not3: practical animal-handling/feeding/housing training followed by an individual placement, reports and presentation. AnimalBehaviour is3EC, not6; it includes Tinbergen questions, observation/analysis and scientific reporting. Exact current chemistry/genetics/quantitative/skills modules replace inaccurate generic old labels and supposed first-year integration.

AnimalNutrition includes requirements/metabolism, diet processing/formulation, feed/faeces chemical analysis and live broiler/fish work. Breeding includes designing/optimising a dairy-sheep breeding programme. Reproduction includes species-specific fertility and technologies; Aquaculture concerns cultivation physiology. These remain specialist gaps despite real UCR mechanism/ecology contributions.

Current profile/module catalogue sufficiently establishes the full selected pathway and progress conditions. The published2025scheme is historical. The publicly found thesis guide labels itself2020–2021, despite recent search metadata; it is not used to override current requirements or create an additional approval gate.
